inputs.original_text: Earlier this month, an Indiana judge blocked a prolife law, arguing that limiting abortion violates freedom of religion. The claim, brought by the American Civil Liberties Union and Hoosier Jews for Choice, argued that an Indiana law “violates religious freedoms by burdening the ability to obtain an abortion in accordance with their sincerely held beliefs.” Judge Christina R. [...] The post This Judge Thinks Killing Babies in Abortions is a Religious Right appeared first on LifeNews.com .
inputs.modified_text: An Indiana judge has blocked a law restricting abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice framed the restriction as a burden on religious belief. That turns religious liberty into a weapon against the state’s responsibility to protect unborn life. No one’s freedom is unlimited, and calling abortion access “care” doesn’t erase the moral stakes or the interests of the most vulnerable. The real question is whether the law may uphold a society’s duty to defend life—not whether bodily autonomy should always trump it.
